analysis: The gated preference branch succeeded in this trial: host validation macro HR@10 reached 0.5375, up 0.0238 from the supplied previous score of 0.5137. Category HR@10 was 0.595 for Movies_and_TV, 0.555 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.435 for Electronics, and 0.565 for CDs_and_Vinyl. Electronics improved by 0.025 over the previous 0.410 and by 0.015 over the stated baseline 0.420. These results support retaining the architecture for further validation, but one trial does not establish why it improved or demonstrate robustness across seeds. The host reported successful execution using 216.18 allocated GPU-seconds.
code_summary: SASRec adds a causal preference branch that computes padding-masked cumulative means of raw item embeddings within the truncated input window. A learned linear projection and LayerNorm transform these means, then a feature-wise sigmoid gate blends them with normalized Transformer features. Gate weights start at zero and bias at -2, initially favoring Transformer features. Training retains uniform positive-plus-64-negative cross-entropy, candidate embedding scores, item biases, and existing optimization settings. Saved metadata and the generated predictor reconstruct and strictly load the same architecture with routing for all four datasets. The code includes checks for padding safety, causality, branch gradients, and checkpoint/predictor score agreement.
